explanation: C requires explicit declaration of variable types before use.  This allows the compiler to allocate appropriate memory and perform type checking, enhancing code reliability and efficiency.  Declarations specify the type (e.g., integer, float, character), storage class (e.g., automatic, static), and optionally qualifiers (e.g., const, volatile).
example_explanation: This example demonstrates various data type declarations in C.  `int`, `float`, and `char` declare variables of different numeric and character types. `const` prevents modification of `PI` after initialization. `static` allocates memory for `count` only once and retains its value between function calls.
